The probable joke (inferred, not stated): the baby says 'a week ago' while being a newborn, so he is describing his dad poking the pregnant belly. The on-screen 'One day he'll find out' is not explained in the clip.

solo_route.how: 1) Start from a still of LumeBook's own illustrated baby or toddler hero (a fictional child, or one with written parental consent), vertical 9:16, swaddled or in a cosy crib, with empty space at the top for text. 2) Run image-to-video: slow push-in, eyes drift toward camera-right, mouth moves as if talking, 6 to 8 seconds; generate 3 to 5 takes and keep the one where the face morphs the least. If the generator will not draw a hand with a mic cleanly, add a simple mic cutout in CapCut instead. 3) Write a two-line gag (interviewer question plus the baby's answer, about 15 to 20 words), record it yourself and pitch it up, or use a stock synthetic voice that is not a clone of a real person, then trim the clip so the mouth is moving while the words play. 4) Put one short Hebrew teaser line in the top third from frame 0 and add a 1-second LumeBook end card on the last frame. Budget about 1 to 2 hours.
solo_route.needs: Nothing, as long as the baby is LumeBook's illustrated hero and the joke does not use a real customer's baby photo.

evidence_notes: OBSERVED: single locked-off shot of a newborn in a hospital bed, one hand with a small clip-on mic appearing from 1.0 s, one line of white text present in every frame, black letterbox bars. Possible AI cues in the frames: the baby's skin is very smooth and evenly lit with no visible blotches or peeling; the face shape and eye shape shift noticeably between 0.0, 3.0 and 6.0 s (forehead and nose bridge change, eyes go from slits to open to shut); the background is generic and soft-focus with a cinematic colour grade. The hand and fingers on the mic look plausible in the sampled frames and I found no extra fingers, but I only see one frame per second, so I cannot rule out hand glitches between frames. From stills alone I cannot prove the clip is AI; the meta field ai_made_how says ai_generated from the search, and ai_tools says 'tagged #ai' but the caption field is empty, so I could not see that tag. No tool is named in the frames or transcript. SPOKEN: Whisper gave two clear English segments (0.0 to 1.92 and 1.92 to 7.92); medium reliability, but the exact word timing is coarse. I cannot hear the voice, so I cannot say whether it is synthetic, a human voice-over, or a pitched voice. INFERRED: the 'a week ago' joke reading (dad poking the belly) and that the baby's mouth movement is generated lip movement. made_by is unclear: no caption, no credit, and the channel median of 268 views means I cannot tell whether this is the account's own generation or a re-upload of someone else's clip. LIKENESS AND CONSENT: no identifiable real child or celebrity that I can see; the risk is a photoreal newborn in a hospital setting that could be taken for real footage (label it as AI per platform rules). For LumeBook, never animate a customer's real baby photo into a talking joke without explicit written parental consent, and do not clone a real person's voice.
